evals.prompt: Put together this week's threat-intel digest for the team — I want AI discoveries, in-the-wild stuff, malware families, and the vendor delta.
evals.expected_output: Five concurrent VDB calls (ai-discoveries, ai-in-wild, ai-malware, exploit-trends, vendor-trends), rendered as a five-section digest each capped at 5 rows, plus a repo overlay section. No memory writes.
expectations: Reads .vulnetix/capabilities.yaml and uses derived.primary_package_manager to default the --ecosystem filter

Issues five parallel Bash calls: `vulnetix vdb ai-discoveries -o json --limit 20`, `vulnetix vdb ai-in-wild -o json --limit 20`, `vulnetix vdb ai-malware -o json --limit 10`, `vulnetix vdb exploit-trends -o json`, `vulnetix vdb vendor-trends -o json`
Pipes the three AI endpoints through skills/_lib/jq/ai-list.jq rather than dumping raw payloads

Renders five sections (Newly discovered, Active in the wild, Malware families, Exploit trends, Vendor trends) each capped at 5 rows, with the exploit-trends section as a Mermaid pie/bar chart by severity tier
Adds a sixth Concerns for this repo section marking In repo? for affected packages against lockfiles, and writes nothing to memory.yaml

evals.prompt: Microsoft has been busy lately — give me the threat feed filtered to vendor=microsoft so I can see what's trending for them.
evals.expected_output: Vendor-filtered digest with --vendor microsoft passed through each supporting AI endpoint, five sections rendered, vendor-trends month-over-month delta highlighted. Read-only.
expectations: Passes `--vendor microsoft` through to each VDB call where supported (ai-discoveries, ai-in-wild, ai-malware, vendor-trends)
Notes that the vendor field name varies across endpoints (vendor / vendorProject / productVendor) and relies on the ai-list.jq filter normalising to .package // .family
Renders the Vendor trends section as top 5 vendors by month-over-month CVE delta with Microsoft positioned in the ranking
Caps each of the five sections at 5 rows and produces the Concerns for this repo overlay against the lockfile
Performs no .vulnetix/memory.yaml writes (the skill is read-only)

evals.prompt: I want a compact daily scan of novel AI-discovered vulns and AI-authored malware families relevant to our Python stack.
evals.expected_output: Ecosystem-filtered (--ecosystem pypi) parallel fetch from the five VDB endpoints, digest rendered with focus on AI-discoveries and AI-malware sections, repo overlay against requirements/poetry lockfile.
expectations: Determines ecosystem pypi from derived.primary_package_manager and passes `--ecosystem pypi` to each call that supports it
Runs the five vulnetix vdb calls (ai-discoveries, ai-in-wild, ai-malware, exploit-trends, vendor-trends) in parallel and pipes the AI-family ones through ai-list.jq
Renders the Newly discovered (AI researchers) section with CVE, package, CVSS, researcher columns and the Malware families section with family / package targets / severity
Notes that vdb ai-malware covers AI-authored OR AI-runtime-targeted families and uses the .family field to disambiguate
Marks In repo? for each item by grepping requirements.txt / poetry.lock / Pipfile.lock and writes nothing to memory.yaml
